story.title: Was Elon Musk the US midterms' biggest loser? – Stateside with Kai and Carter
story.summary: The tech industry spent big on the midterms, but it turned out to be a poor investment. Elon Musk poured a staggering $446m dollars into Republican-aligned political action committees (Pacs) and groups since last year, but his efforts didn’t pay off. Democrats won every one of the five Senate races where Musk’s America Pac spent the most money backing Republican candidates. Carter Sherman and Kai Wright are joined by the Guardian’s US tech editor, Blake Montgomery , to ask what the ‘blue tsunami’ will mean for Musk and the wider tech industry. linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
Binance is currently working to recover $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency following a massive security breach. The company says hackers gained access by targeting a developer with a tampered installer via a malicious Google ad back in June. They then used fake job interviews and an internal AI tool to execute what is now considered the largest crypto theft in history. Security experts have linked the attack to North Korean hackers.

In the U.S., financial markets are reacting to the outcome of the midterm elections. Investors responded to the Democratic victories by pushing U.S. stocks higher while the dollar saw a decline. Government bond yields also fell as markets adjusted to the news.

This shift in the political landscape has raised questions about the economic outlook for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency. Economists are now watching how the loss of Republican control in Congress might impact inflation, interest rates, and overall global economic growth.

slides.headline: Paraguay's President Impeached Minutes After Resigning
slides.subtitle: The lower house voted unanimously for impeachment on Thursday.

slides.explanation: Millions of people were suddenly locked out of their own bank accounts. That is roughly the size of a mid-sized nation unable to access their savings.

slides.headline: Resignation did not stop the impeachment
slides.explanation: Peña announced he was stepping down on social media, but the lower house voted to impeach him just minutes later.
This report is verified by three independent outlets including France 24, NPR World, and BBC World. Their consensus confirms the timeline of this legislative action.

instagram.caption:
Paraguay is in political turmoil.

President Santiago Peña has resigned and was impeached by the lower house in the same hour.

The move follows widespread protests sparked by a banking crisis. Millions of citizens were left unable to access their money after a bank takeover.

Lawmakers voted unanimously to remove him from office immediately after his resignation announcement on social media. How do you think a country stabilizes after such a sudden leadership vacuum?

story.title: Paraguay's president Peña impeached moments after resigning over banking scandal
story.summary: Paraguay’s lower house voted unanimously to impeach President Santiago Peña on Thursday, just minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Peña blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.

story_card.headline: Elon Musk's $446 Million Midterm Bet Fails
story_card.standfirst: The tech billionaire poured massive funds into Republican groups, but saw little return.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Elon Musk spent $446 million on Republican groups. Yet, Democrats won every Senate race he targeted.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The tech industry spent heavily on the midterms. It was an attempt to influence election outcomes.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Huge political spending does not guarantee results. This shows money cannot always buy elections.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for future tech industry spending patterns. We will see if donors change their strategies.

story_card.caption:
Elon Musk spent over 400 million dollars on US midterm elections but saw limited success for his investments.

Despite record-breaking spending from the tech sector, the results were underwhelming. Democrats swept the five key Senate races where Musk's money was most active. It highlights the limits of political influence through direct funding.

Do you think big money in politics actually changes how people vote?
